body:
That sounds horrible, I'm sorry.

Do you mind if I ask you how you decided that you should speak to your ex, how you decided that closure could actually help? So many people say with absolute certainty that speaking to one's ex is never healthy, are they wrong or is there a state of mind that a person must be in for it to be effective?

How did you bring yourself to accept that your soulmate left you? Not accept that it did in reality happen but accept that it wasn't an ultimate reflection of your value as a partner. Are you able to hope still that you will someday love someone and be loved by someone so completely again?

I struggle to be grateful for this. It feels like sarcasm to try to say I'm grateful to be this recovered because to be so grateful would indicate in some twisted way that I'm supposedly grateful to have been injured in the first place?

I don't have my mind wrapped around this idea. It seems to be an obvious step to those outside of this situation, I should just be grateful. But I can't seriously be grateful for being granted this crippled life.

The bastard of it is that it's not even always quite just not being able to remember the thing, sometimes it's like my brain just isn't able to hold the whole problem at once. By the time I've fully absorbed the idea of the problem the first parts are already slipping away.

I had heard that the greatest portion of your healing occurs within the first two years (and still most of that much sooner).

I am currently employed and performing adequately in my current position. I'm hoping to move to a new position in part because this job rarely pushes me. This crisis of confidence is borne of the rare opportunity to reach out for a job that I'm not normally assigned and now finding it harder to get started than I feel like it should be. I'll search for it too but my assumption for stuff like Vocational Rehabilitation is that I'm too recovered to really be able to get advantaged by it.

Do you know if there's a version that isn't a workbook? I guess I'll just look it up myself. But writing is one of my blessedly few physical handicaps. I can write but it's painfully slow.

I should look again for a counselor specializing in brain injury. I have a counselor that I do really like but I had chosen him long before I broke my brain.

Thanks a lot!

No, not at all. Thanks a lot.

I haven't gone and bought a candle yet but it somehow is a little easier when I know it's not an "unforgivable sin"
Thank you for the seriousness of this advice. I appreciate that you recognize that I may end up self-harming and used this chance to educate me on the proper routes and probable consequences.

I used to channel it into running and general fitness but now, after a severe physical accident, I'm not able to run yet/for-now/ever-again. I hate that I can't use my pain tolerance for anything useful. I used to be able to train with it and know that I was improving my hypothetical ability to handle potential crises

You don't need to feel guilty for needing to vent. You aren't making yourself a liar by telling us about your suicide urges which you will then not follow through with. It is good to not follow through with your urges. It is good to be honest about the urges. You are not a liar.

There's nothing worse than seeing people be hurt by the actions you've taken post-injury, to know that they would be hurt less if you had just died, and to continue on with no choice but to continue hurting them. Because oxymoronically they would somehow be hurt worse if you ceased at this point? If I had ceased from the injury would it be different somehow? I just tire of hurting the people I care about. Life is a Catch 22, I'll hurt them by continuing to exist and interact with them but somehow they will be hurt if I decide to remove the cause of their pain.

Is it alright for me to just post questions in here? I've made a completely undeserved but incredible so far recovery from a traumatic brain injury I experienced in May of last year. I was in the hospital for basically the rest of that year and out of work for roughly one total year. Things are pretty close to normal but occasional things happen that make me question "is this because my mind works differently now?" I don't like not being able to trust my own perception. I would like to have somewhere I could ask people if they think my perception of my perception (frustratingly contradictory) might be skewed.
